raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. Each rollout worker reports what it loads (pipeline stage, resident experts and, for vLLM TP>1, its slice of each tensor) and receives only that. The bucket layout is built on the first sync and cached, so later syncs send no per-tensor metadata. Design: `docs/advance/sharded_nixl_weight_sync.md`.

Related work: #7108 does Megatron-to-SGLang P2P over Mooncake; the NCCL M2N stack (#7432, #7552, #8087, #8088) has the same goal over NCCL collectives. This PR uses NIXL one-sided writes into vLLM and supports FSDP and Megatron trainers.

### Results (8x B300 nodes, RoCE)

| Model, trainer to vLLM | `nccl` | `nixl` | `sharded_nixl` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/CP=2/EP=8 (16 GPUs) to vLLM TP=16/EP=16 (16 GPUs) | 21.7 s | 21.1 s | **6.35 s** |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B, Megatron TP=4/PP=4/CP=2/EP=8 (32 GPUs) to vLLM TP=16/EP=16 (16 GPUs) | 21.5 s | 19.8 s | **6.36 s** |
| GRPO, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/EP=4 to 2 x vLLM TP=4/EP=4 | 9.4 s | 9.3 s | **7.5 s** |
| GRPO, Qwen3-0.6B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2 to 4 x vLLM TP=2 | **3.3 s** | | 6.1 s |

- 235B: standalone harness (not in this PR), mean of syncs 2 to 4; vLLM's greedy output is checked against reference tokens after every sync. Measured with slice hashing off.
- GRPO: `tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh` on GSM8K, median `update_weights` over 6 steps; rollout-vs-trainer log-prob agreement matches `nccl` and `nixl`.
- `nixl` and `nccl` stream the whole model from trainer rank 0. On small dense models the per-sync overhead dominates and `nccl` stays faster.

### Test

Environment: 8x B300, NIXL 1.4.1 (UCX), vLLM 0.24.0 (not yet run on 0.32.0, which verl pins; the new CI step runs there).

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_nixl_layout_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_delta.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_block_placement.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_global_steps_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py` | 189 passed |
| `SHARDED_NIXL_MOE_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen3-30B-A3B dir> pytest -s tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_nixl_on_gpu.py` | 13 passed |
| `RANK_LOCAL_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen3-0.6B or Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct dir> pytest -s tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_rank_local_bake.py` | 1 passed each |

The GPU tests run FSDP and Megatron trainers against mock rollout workers that check every received weight bit-exact: 1 to 1, 2 to 2 and 2 to 6 workers, GPU and pinned-host staging, MoE expert ownership, TP=2 rank-local slices, and the failure paths (corrupted slice, sync-id mismatch, retry after a mid-sync failure). The bake test runs a real vLLM TP=2 engine and is added to `vllm.yml`.

### Usage

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    checkpoint_engine:
      backend: sharded_nixl
      update_weights_bucket_megabytes: 512
      engine_kwargs:
        sharded_nixl:
          device: cuda             # staging buffers: cuda (GPUDirect RDMA) or cpu (pinned host)
          rollout_dtype: bfloat16
```

Requires `pip install nixl` and a separate rollout (tested with v1 `separate_async`).

### Code

Four commits, one per layer, then the RFC; easiest to review one by one:

1. `[ckpt, rollout]` opt-in hooks, both off by default so existing backends are unchanged: `send_weights_takes_engine` (the engine gets the training engine instead of an all-gathered iterator; `delta_sharded` now uses it too) and `needs_rollout_layout`, plus `BaseRollout.get_weight_ownership()`, implemented for vLLM.
2. `[ckpt]` the engine: ownership filtering, cached layout and write tables, per-slice hashes checked before any weight is applied, and fail-closed retry (generation cannot resume after a partial sync until a retry completes).
3. `[megatron, ckpt]` `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard`: each rank's local shards in HF coordinates, with no duplicate sends across DP or expert-DP replicas.
4. `[rollout]` vLLM rank-local TP slices, taken from a dry run of vLLM's own `load_weights` instead of per-model rules.

### Known limitations

- The fail-closed marker lives in `CheckpointEngineManager`; the `fully_async` rollouter's rebalance resumes replicas directly and bypasses it.
- Tested end to end with v1 `separate_async`, the loop verl's CI uses since #7357; `fully_async`, `one_step_off` and SGLang have not been run.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/advance/sharded_nixl_weight_sync.md` and `verl/checkpoint_engine/README.md`.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows): the CPU tests and the bake test run in CI; `test_sharded_nixl_on_gpu.py` skips there until CI installs NIXL.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1).
- [x] Not related to the recipe submodule.

### AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude, in Cursor) was used for the code, the tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

@rafiw Thanks for your contribution. As we're focusing on low precision rollout, there're more edge cases to handle in P2P weight reshard. During weight refit, weights are designed to be quantized in trainer size and export `(weight, scale)` to rollout. https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/low_precision/qat.html While in P2P weight reshard, weights have to be quantized on local shard, but the quantization block(e.g MXFP8/MXFP4 1x32, NVFP4 32x32) maybe across TP ranks, so we have to do additional communication to sync `amax` for those blocks. For verification, I suggest to test `sharded_nixl` on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, which is a mixed mxfp8+mxfp4 low precision model.

Thanks @wuxibin89 for the review and for pointing me to the low-precision path, I missed it when tested the engine.

Right now sharded_nixl doesn't run the trainer-side WeightQuantizer: it is applied only in MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param, and sharded_nixl exports through the shard APIs instead. With a quantized rollout it would send BF16 weights and no scales.

delta_sharded has the same gap, and #8369 made it fail at startup in dispatch_rollout_weight_quantizer. Can I extend that check to sharded_nixl in this PR, so the PR can move forward for BF16 rollouts and quantization support follows in a separate PR? Or do you consider quantization support a blocker for this PR?

How would you like this solved? What we have in mind:

For params the rollout quantizer quantizes and that are split across trainer ranks (TP, or ETP for experts): gather the param inside its TP/ETP group to one rank, run the existing _rollout_weight_quantizer on the full HF tensor, and send (weight, scale) from that rank. Params already whole on a rank (TP=1, experts with ETP=1) are quantized locally. Everything else keeps the local-shard path, with no PP/EP/DP gather.
Reusing the existing quantizer gives the same bytes as the current all-gather path for every format it supports, so no per-format amax sync is needed. [ckpt, megatron, sglang] fix: preserve DSv4 FP8 delta fidelity #7676 takes the amax-sync route for DeepSeek-V4 FP8 in delta_sharded; the gather looks simpler to us, and costs one gather inside the TP group (usually NVLink), only for quantized layers.
The rollout side stays as is: vLLM loads the pre-quantized tensors as it does from nixl.
DeepSeek-V4: Megatron-Bridge quantizes inside its own converter, so split params there would go through the bridge's conversion with only the TP gather kept. Then I'd validate on DeepSeek-V4-Flash as you suggested.
What do you think?

**Handle interrupted vLLM weight streams.** `BucketedWeightReceiver.receive_weights` blocks on `self.socket.recv_pyobj()` and exits only after it receives a bucket with `is_last=True`. It has no abort message or receive timeout. `BucketedWeightSender.async_send_weights` only closes its socket in `finally`. If the sharded engine raises while producing the stream, such as during bucket verification, the sender can stop before sending the terminal bucket. The vLLM receiver can then remain blocked waiting for another bucket. `ServerAdapter.update_weights` awaits that receiver future after the sender completes, so the update and its retry can remain blocked. Add an explicit abort protocol that `BucketedWeightReceiver` handles, or make the receiver use a bounded timeout and propagate the interrupted transfer as an error.

+"""``sharded_nixl``: ownership-aware trainer -> rollout weight sync over NIXL WRITE.
+
+Every trainer rank exports only the shards it holds (``engine.get_per_tensor_param_shard`` or,
+for Megatron, ``get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard``) and WRITEs them into each generator's
+registered bucket buffers; there is no trainer-side all-gather. Each generator reports its
+``RolloutLayout`` and receives only the parameters it loads. The bucket layout follows from the
+rank-identical export order, so it is built once and cached on the generators by digest.
+Planning lives in ``sharded_nixl_layout``.
+
+Per-sync protocol (S = sync id, NB staging buffers per worker)::
+
+    generator g -> every trainer:   hello{S, rollout layout, cached layout/plan digests}   (ZMQ)
+    trainer 0   -> every generator: sync{S, layout digest, num_buckets [, full layout]}     (ZMQ)
+    trainer r   -> generator g:     plan{S, plan key, tables[k] = [(dst, len)...]}  if g lacks it (ZMQ)
+    for bucket k:
+        trainer r: wait ACK(S, k-NB) from every g; pack own slices into send_buf[k % NB];
+                   NIXL WRITE slices -> g.recv_buf[k % NB] with notif SNX{S,k,r,hashes}
+        generator: wait SNX from all trainers; verify hashes; yield tensors of bucket k;
+                   send_notif ACK{S,k} to every trainer
+
+When every generator advertises ``rank_local_named_tensors`` with slice tables of the same local
+shapes, the sync uses a second layout built from those local (box) shapes and each generator
+receives only its TP slice of each tensor.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import hashlib
+import json
+import logging

This is pre-existing for every backend, but sharded_nixl reaches it on its retry path (a checksum failure inside the stream, or prepare cancelling a stale receive). 
Fixed: on any exception or cancellation after the buffer handshake, the sender sends an abort marker and waits up to 10 s for the ack; the receiver raises and acks after releasing its buffer. Covered by test_sender_failure_aborts_receiver.

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Every trainer rank (FSDP or Megatron) exports only the shards it holds and NIXL-WRITEs them into the rollout workers' staging buffers. Each rollout worker reports what it loads (pipeline stage, resident experts and, for vLLM TP>1, its slice of each tensor) and receives only that. The bucket layout is built on the first sync and cached, so later syncs send no per-tensor metadata. Design: `docs/advance/sharded_nixl_weight_sync.md`.

Related work: #7108 does Megatron-to-SGLang P2P over Mooncake; the NCCL M2N stack (#7432, #7552, #8087, #8088) has the same goal over NCCL collectives. This PR uses NIXL one-sided writes into vLLM and supports FSDP and Megatron trainers.

### Results (8x B300 nodes, RoCE)

| Model, trainer to vLLM | `nccl` | `nixl` | `sharded_nixl` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/CP=2/EP=8 (16 GPUs) to vLLM TP=16/EP=16 (16 GPUs) | 21.7 s | 21.1 s | **6.35 s** |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B, Megatron TP=4/PP=4/CP=2/EP=8 (32 GPUs) to vLLM TP=16/EP=16 (16 GPUs) | 21.5 s | 19.8 s | **6.36 s** |
| GRPO, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/EP=4 to 2 x vLLM TP=4/EP=4 | 9.4 s | 9.3 s | **7.5 s** |
| GRPO, Qwen3-0.6B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2 to 4 x vLLM TP=2 | **3.3 s** | | 6.1 s |

- 235B: standalone harness (not in this PR), mean of syncs 2 to 4; vLLM's greedy output is checked against reference tokens after every sync. Measured with slice hashing off.
- GRPO: `tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh` on GSM8K, median `update_weights` over 6 steps; rollout-vs-trainer log-prob agreement matches `nccl` and `nixl`.
- `nixl` and `nccl` stream the whole model from trainer rank 0. On small dense models the per-sync overhead dominates and `nccl` stays faster.

### Test

Environment: 8x B300, NIXL 1.4.1 (UCX), vLLM 0.24.0 (not yet run on 0.32.0, which verl pins; the new CI step runs there).

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_nixl_layout_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_delta.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_block_placement.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_global_steps_on_cpu.py tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py` | 189 passed |
| `SHARDED_NIXL_MOE_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen3-30B-A3B dir> pytest -s tests/checkpoint_engine/test_sharded_nixl_on_gpu.py` | 13 passed |
| `RANK_LOCAL_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen3-0.6B or Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct dir> pytest -s tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_rank_local_bake.py` | 1 passed each |

The GPU tests run FSDP and Megatron trainers against mock rollout workers that check every received weight bit-exact: 1 to 1, 2 to 2 and 2 to 6 workers, GPU and pinned-host staging, MoE expert ownership, TP=2 rank-local slices, and the failure paths (corrupted slice, sync-id mismatch, retry after a mid-sync failure). The bake test runs a real vLLM TP=2 engine and is added to `vllm.yml`.

### Usage

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    checkpoint_engine:
      backend: sharded_nixl
      update_weights_bucket_megabytes: 512
      engine_kwargs:
        sharded_nixl:
          device: cuda             # staging buffers: cuda (GPUDirect RDMA) or cpu (pinned host)
          rollout_dtype: bfloat16
```

Requires `pip install nixl` and a separate rollout (tested with v1 `separate_async`).

### Code

Four commits, one per layer, then the RFC; easiest to review one by one:

1. `[ckpt, rollout]` opt-in hooks, both off by default so existing backends are unchanged: `send_weights_takes_engine` (the engine gets the training engine instead of an all-gathered iterator; `delta_sharded` now uses it too) and `needs_rollout_layout`, plus `BaseRollout.get_weight_ownership()`, implemented for vLLM.
2. `[ckpt]` the engine: ownership filtering, cached layout and write tables, per-slice hashes checked before any weight is applied, and fail-closed retry (generation cannot resume after a partial sync until a retry completes).
3. `[megatron, ckpt]` `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard`: each rank's local shards in HF coordinates, with no duplicate sends across DP or expert-DP replicas.
4. `[rollout]` vLLM rank-local TP slices, taken from a dry run of vLLM's own `load_weights` instead of per-model rules.

### Known limitations

- The fail-closed marker lives in `CheckpointEngineManager`; the `fully_async` rollouter's rebalance resumes replicas directly and bypasses it.
- Tested end to end with v1 `separate_async`, the loop verl's CI uses since #7357; `fully_async`, `one_step_off` and SGLang have not been run.

+# Sharded NIXL Weight Sync
+
+Last updated: 10/22/2026.
+
+RFC for the ``sharded_nixl`` checkpoint engine: trainer-to-rollout weight sync in which every trainer rank
+writes the shards it holds straight into the rollout workers' buffers over NIXL, with no trainer-side
+all-gather. Code: ``verl/checkpoint_engine/sharded_nixl_checkpoint_engine.py`` (protocol),
+``sharded_nixl_layout.py`` (planning) and ``verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/rank_local_bake.py`` (vLLM
+TP slices).
+
+## Motivation
+
+In a disaggregated setup (``hybrid_engine=False``) every step ends with a full weight sync. The ``nccl``
+and ``nixl`` engines all-gather full tensors on the trainer and send the whole model from trainer rank 0
+to every rollout worker. Two costs follow:
+
+- **One sender.** The sync is bounded by rank 0's gather and link, so a larger trainer does not make it
+  faster: at Qwen3-235B-A22B both engines take ~20 s whether the trainer has 16 or 32 GPUs.
+- **Everything to everyone.** Every rollout worker receives every parameter, although with rollout EP it
+  loads only its experts, with PP only its layers, and with TP only a slice of each tensor.
+
+The weights are already sharded on the trainer; ``sharded_nixl`` keeps them sharded on the wire.
+
+## Design
+
+``sharded_nixl`` is a ``CheckpointEngine`` backend, so it plugs into the same
+``CheckpointEngineManager`` -> ``CheckpointEngineWorker`` flow as the other engines.
+
+**Export.** The engine takes the training engine in ``send_weights(engine, global_steps)`` and exports
+each rank's local shards: ``get_per_tensor_param_shard()`` for FSDP (a ``Shard(0)`` or replicated shard
+is one byte interval of the flattened tensor) and ``get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard()`` for Megatron (local
+shards in final HF coordinates, reusing the ``delta_sharded`` Megatron-Bridge probe). Nothing is sent
+twice: TP-sharded Megatron parameters come from data-parallel rank 0 only, and replicated experts
+round-robin over the expert-data-parallel group.
+
+**Ownership.** Before the first sync every rollout worker reports a ``RolloutLayout`` through
+``BaseRollout.get_weight_ownership()``: TP/PP/EP ranks, layer range, resident experts and accepted wire
+formats. The engine drops what a worker does not load, and expands fused MoE tensors into the per-expert
+HF names vLLM loads. A rollout that returns ``None`` receives everything.
+
+**Static layout.** Every trainer rank exports the same ``(name, shape, dtype)`` sequence, so all ranks
+compute the same bucket layout without communicating. The rollout side caches the layout and each trainer
+rank's write tables by digest, so after the first sync a sync exchanges only small headers.
+
+**Transport.** Per sync (S = sync id, NB staging buffers per worker):
+
+```text
+rollout worker g -> every trainer rank: hello{S, rollout layout, cached digests}     (ZMQ)
+trainer rank 0   -> every worker:       sync{S, layout digest, num_buckets}           (ZMQ)
+for bucket k:
+    trainer rank r: wait ACK(S, k-NB) from every worker; pack its slices into buffer k % NB;
+                    NIXL WRITE them into every worker's buffer k % NB with notification SNX{S, k, r, hashes}
+    worker g:       wait SNX from every trainer rank; check hashes; load bucket k; send ACK{S, k}
+```
+
+Writes are one-sided, so there is no NCCL group between trainer and rollout and every trainer rank sends
+in parallel. Staging buffers live in GPU memory (GPUDirect RDMA) or pinned host memory.
+
+**Rank-local TP slices.** When every rollout worker advertises ``rank_local_named_tensors`` with a table
+of the slices it keeps, the engine plans a second layout over those local shapes, and each TP rank
+receives only its slices; pieces that several workers need are packed once. The slices come from vLLM
+itself: a dry run of ``model.load_weights`` feeds each checkpoint tensor as a storage-less stand-in that
+records ``narrow()`` calls and catches the final ``copy_``. A name copied as one strict sub-box of one
+parameter gets a slice; anything else is sent whole and goes through ``load_weights``. Received slices
+are copied straight into their parameter views.
+
+**Integrity and failure.** Every written slice carries a 64-bit hash, checked on the rollout side before
+any weight is applied, and sync ids must match. A sync that fails part-way leaves a mix of old and new
+weights, so ``CheckpointEngineManager`` keeps ``resume_generation_replicas`` raising until a later
+``update_weights`` completes; every sync is dense, so that retry repairs every weight. Before the retry,
+``prepare`` cancels the failed sync's leftover send or receive and drops its stale notifications.
+
+**API.** Two opt-in ``CheckpointEngine`` class attributes, both ``False`` by default:
+``send_weights_takes_engine`` (``send_weights`` gets the training engine instead of an all-gathered
+iterator; ``delta_sharded`` now uses it too) and ``needs_rollout_layout`` (the worker's ``RolloutLayout``
+goes to ``set_rollout_layout`` before the first receive). ``BaseRollout.get_weight_ownership()`` returns
+``None`` by default; the vLLM ``ServerAdapter`` implements it.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **NCCL resharding (#7432, #7552, #8087, #8088).** The same goal, each worker receiving only its
+  destination shards, over NCCL collectives between trainer and rollout. #8087 uses the same
+  ``rank_local_named_tensors`` wire format name, so the two vLLM receive paths could be shared.
+- **Mooncake P2P (#7108).** Per-rank RDMA writes from Megatron to SGLang over Mooncake. This RFC targets
+  vLLM over NIXL and also supports FSDP trainers.
+- **Sparse deltas (``delta_sharded``).** Orthogonal: it shrinks what is sent, not who sends it, and still
+  funnels through rank 0. Combining the two is future work.
+
+## Measured results
+
+B300 nodes, 400 Gb/s RoCE, GPUDirect RDMA, NIXL 1.4.1 (UCX), vLLM 0.24.0, 512 MB buckets.
+
+| Setup | ``nixl`` | ``nccl`` | ``sharded_nixl`` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Qwen3-235B-A22B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/CP=2/EP=8 (16 GPUs) to vLLM TP=16/EP=16 (16 GPUs) | 21.1 s | 21.7 s | **6.35 s** |
+| Same, trainer TP=4/PP=4/CP=2/EP=8 (32 GPUs) | 19.8 s | 21.5 s | **6.36 s** |
+| GRPO, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Megatron TP=4/PP=2/EP=4 to 2 x vLLM TP=4/EP=4 | 9.3 s | 9.4 s | **7.5 s** |
+
+The 235B rows come from a standalone benchmark that checks vLLM's greedy output against reference tokens
+after every sync; they were measured before slice hashing became mandatory, with it off. The GRPO row is the median ``update_weights`` time over 6 steps of
+``tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh`` on GSM8K, where rollout-vs-trainer log-prob agreement
+matched ``nccl`` and ``nixl``. At 235B the network is far from saturated (~87 GB/s across 16 workers);
+most of the sync is the rollout side loading each bucket into vLLM.
+
+## Usage
+
+```yaml
+actor_rollout_ref:
+  rollout:
+    checkpoint_engine:
+      backend: sharded_nixl
+      update_weights_bucket_megabytes: 512
+      engine_kwargs:
+        sharded_nixl:
+          device: cuda             # staging buffers: cuda (GPUDirect RDMA) or cpu (pinned host)
+          rollout_dtype: bfloat16  # wire dtype of floating-point weights; match the rollout dtype
+          ownership: adapter       # send each rollout worker only what it loads; "all" sends everything
+```
+
+It needs ``pip install nixl`` (tested with 1.4.1) and a trainer mode with a separate rollout, such as v1
+``separate_async``.
+
+## Limitations and roadmap
+
+- Rank-local slices need vLLM with plain bf16, TP>1 and a local checkpoint; quantization, LoRA,
+  speculative decoding and PP fall back to full tensors.
+- The fail-closed marker lives in ``CheckpointEngineManager``, so a replica resumed through another
+  handle (the ``fully_async`` rollouter's rebalance) bypasses it; moving it onto the rollout server actors
+  would close that gap.
+- Tested with FSDP and Megatron trainers, vLLM rollout and v1 ``separate_async``; SGLang, ``fully_async``
+  and ``one_step_off`` are untested.
+- On small dense models the per-sync overhead dominates and ``nccl`` stays faster; this is not investigated
+  yet.
+- verl CI does not install NIXL, so the GPU tests skip there; the planning code has CPU tests, and the vLLM
+  bake test runs in the vLLM CI job.

+def test_mcore_shard_runs_replay_nan_probe_order():
+    """Cached source runs (``lidx=None``) must reproduce the NaN probe's values in
+    the same slot-major HF order without returning indices."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from verl.workers.engine.megatron.delta_export import McoreParamExport, _nan_block, mcore_hf_delta_entry

+"""CPU tests of the ``sharded_nixl`` bucket layout and write planning (``sharded_nixl_layout``)."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.sharded_nixl_layout import (
+    BoxSegment,
+    BucketLayout,
+    LayoutBuilder,
+    ParamEntry,
+    build_bucket_layout,
+    clip_segments,
+    contribution_range,
+    expand_fused_moe_entry,
+    index_runs,
+    local_entry,
+    local_shapes_key,
+    merge_box_plans,
+    normalize_slices,
+    owned_name_filter,
+    plan_box_writes,
+    plan_indexed_writes,
+    plan_rank_local_indexed_writes,
+    plan_rank_local_writes,
+    plan_writes,
+    slices_digest,
+)
+from verl.workers.engine.fsdp.utils import unfuse_moe_params
+from verl.workers.engine.spec import BlockPlacement, ShardSpec
+from verl.workers.rollout.base import RolloutLayout
+
+BF16 = torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _entries(spec):
+    """``ParamEntry`` list of plain tensors from ``(name, shape, dtype)`` tuples."""
+    return [ParamEntry(n, tuple(s), d, n, 0) for n, s, d in spec]
+
+
+def test_plan_indexed_writes_compacts_runs_across_buckets():
+    builder = LayoutBuilder(bucket_size=8, align=2)
+    entry = ParamEntry("w", (10,), BF16, "source")
+    builder.add(entry)
+    layout = builder.build()
+
+    writes = plan_indexed_writes(layout, [entry], index_runs(torch.tensor([6]), torch.tensor([1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 9])))
+
+    assert [(w.bucket_id, w.dst_offset, w.src_offset, w.length) for w in writes] == [
+        (0, 2, 0, 4),
+        (1, 2, 4, 6),
+        (2, 2, 10, 2),
+    ]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- layout
+
+
+def test_layout_first_fit_and_alignment():
+    bucket = 1024
+    layout = build_bucket_layout(_entries([("a", (100,), BF16), ("b", (100,), BF16), ("c", (300,), BF16)]), bucket, 256)
+    a, b, c = layout.slots
+    assert (a.bucket_id, a.offset) == (0, 0)
+    assert (b.bucket_id, b.offset) == (0, 256)  # 200 bytes -> aligned up to 256
+    assert (c.bucket_id, c.offset) == (1, 0)  # 600 bytes do not fit after 456
+    assert layout.num_buckets == 2
+    assert layout.total_bytes == 1000
+
+
+def test_layout_chunks_tensor_larger_than_bucket():
+    """A tensor larger than a bucket starts a fresh bucket and is cut into bucket-sized chunks."""
+    bucket = 1024
+    layout = build_bucket_layout(
+        _entries([("s", (10,), BF16), ("big", (1500,), BF16), ("t", (10,), BF16)]), bucket, 256
+    )
+    slots = layout.slots_by_name["big"]
+    assert [(s.bucket_id, s.chunk_offset, s.chunk_size, s.offset) for s in slots] == [
+        (1, 0, 1024, 0),
+        (2, 1024, 1024, 0),
+        (3, 2048, 952, 0),
+    ]
+    t = layout.slots_by_name["t"][0]
+    assert (t.bucket_id, t.offset) == (4, 0)  # 952 aligns up to 1024: no room left in bucket 3
+    assert layout.num_buckets == 5
+
+
+def test_layout_duplicate_names_raise():
+    b = LayoutBuilder(1024)
+    b.add(ParamEntry("x", (2,), BF16, "x", 0))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        b.add(ParamEntry("x", (2,), BF16, "x", 0))
+
+
+def test_layout_digest_and_wire_roundtrip():
+    e = _entries([("a", (4, 4), BF16), ("b", (7,), torch.float32)])
+    l1 = build_bucket_layout(e, 4096)
+    l2 = build_bucket_layout(e, 4096)
+    l3 = build_bucket_layout(e, 8192)
+    assert l1.digest == l2.digest != l3.digest
+    rt = BucketLayout.from_wire(l1.to_wire())
+    assert rt.digest == l1.digest and rt.slots == l1.slots and rt.entries == l1.entries
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- MoE expansion
+
+
+def test_expand_fused_moe_matches_unfuse_moe_params():
+    """Every per-expert entry's byte range in the fused tensor equals ``unfuse_moe_params``."""
+    E, inter, H = 4, 6, 5
+    gate_up = torch.randn(E, 2 * inter, H, dtype=BF16)
+    down = torch.randn(E, H, inter, dtype=BF16)
+    named = [("model.layers.0.mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", gate_up), ("model.layers.0.mlp.experts.down_proj", down)]
+    reference = dict(unfuse_moe_params(iter(named), "qwen3_moe"))
+    for src_name, t in named:
+        entries = expand_fused_moe_entry(src_name, tuple(t.shape), t.dtype, "qwen3_moe")
+        flat = t.reshape(-1)
+        assert all(e.name in reference for e in entries)
+        for e in entries:
+            ref = reference[e.name]
+            assert tuple(ref.shape) == e.shape
+            assert torch.equal(flat[e.src_elem_offset : e.src_elem_offset + e.numel].view(e.shape), ref)
+    # gpt_oss keeps the fused layout for inference
+    assert (
+        len(expand_fused_moe_entry("model.layers.0.mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", (E, 2 * inter, H), BF16, "gpt_oss")) == 1
+    )
+    assert expand_fused_moe_entry("model.norm.weight", (H,), BF16, "qwen3_moe")[0].name == "model.norm.weight"
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- contribution range / write planning
+
+
+def _block(full_shape, local_shape, global_offset, contributes=True):
+    return ShardSpec(
+        full_shape=tuple(full_shape),
+        place=BlockPlacement(tuple(local_shape), tuple(global_offset), tuple(full_shape)),
+        contributes=contributes,
+    )
+
+
+def test_contribution_range_shard0_and_replicated():
+    """Shard(0) block, HSDP replica (no contribution), replicated tensor, unsupported dim-1 cut."""
+    itemsize = 2
+    spec = _block((8, 4), (2, 4), (4, 0))  # rank holding rows 4..6 of an 8x4 tensor
+    assert contribution_range(spec, 8, itemsize) == (4 * 4 * itemsize, 8 * itemsize)
+    assert contribution_range(_block((8, 4), (2, 4), (4, 0), contributes=False), 8, itemsize) is None
+    rep = ShardSpec(full_shape=(3, 3), place=0, contributes=True)
+    assert contribution_range(rep, 9, 4) == (0, 36)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError):
+        contribution_range(_block((8, 4), (8, 2), (0, 2)), 16, itemsize)  # dim-1 cut
+
+
+def _simulate(full_tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor], world: int, bucket_size: int, fused_model_type=None, owns=None):
+    """Shard every tensor along dim 0 across ``world`` ranks and apply each rank's planned writes
+    to fake buckets, asserting no two writes overlap. Returns (layout, buckets, entries_by_src)."""
+    entries_by_src = {}
+    builder = LayoutBuilder(bucket_size, 256)
+    for name, t in full_tensors.items():
+        es = expand_fused_moe_entry(name, tuple(t.shape), t.dtype, fused_model_type)
+        entries_by_src[name] = es
+        for e in es:
+            builder.add(e)
+    layout = builder.build()
+    buckets = [bytearray(bucket_size) for _ in range(layout.num_buckets)]
+    written = [bytearray(bucket_size) for _ in range(layout.num_buckets)]
+    for rank in range(world):
+        for name, t in full_tensors.items():
+            rows = t.shape[0]
+            per = (rows + world - 1) // world
+            r0, r1 = min(rank * per, rows), min((rank + 1) * per, rows)
+            if r0 >= r1:
+                continue
+            local = t[r0:r1].contiguous()
+            spec = _block(t.shape, local.shape, (r0,) + (0,) * (t.dim() - 1))
+            rng = contribution_range(spec, local.numel(), t.element_size())
+            u8 = local.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).numpy().tobytes()
+            for s in plan_writes(layout, entries_by_src[name], rng):
+                if owns is not None and not owns(s.name):
+                    continue
+                buckets[s.bucket_id][s.dst_offset : s.dst_offset + s.length] = u8[
+                    s.src_offset : s.src_offset + s.length
+                ]
+                assert not any(written[s.bucket_id][s.dst_offset : s.dst_offset + s.length]), "overlapping writes"
+                written[s.bucket_id][s.dst_offset : s.dst_offset + s.length] = b"\x01" * s.length
+    return layout, buckets, entries_by_src
+
+
+def _reassemble(layout, buckets, name):
+    """Concatenate a tensor's chunks from the fake buckets."""
+    e = layout.entry_by_name[name]
+    raw = bytearray()
+    for s in layout.slots_by_name[name]:
+        raw += buckets[s.bucket_id][s.offset : s.offset + s.chunk_size]
+    return torch.frombuffer(bytes(raw), dtype=e.dtype).view(e.shape) if e.numel else torch.empty(e.shape, dtype=e.dtype)
+

+    """The per-slice checksum is the XOR of the slice's 8-byte words (an 8-bit XOR of its bytes
+    misses swapped bytes) and does not depend on where the slice sits in the buffer."""

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- rank-local (TP) boxes
+#
+# Brute-force reference: fill the full tensor with its own flat indices (torch.arange), so every
+# byte that lands anywhere identifies exactly which source element it came from.
+
+I32 = torch.int32
+
+
+def _gather(src: bytes, segments) -> bytes:
+    """Apply BoxSegments to a rank's local shard bytes (what the engine's pack loop does)."""
+    out = bytearray()
+    for s in segments:
+        for j in range(s.nrows):
+            o = s.src_offset + j * s.stride
+            out += src[o : o + s.row_bytes]
+    return bytes(out)
+
+
+def _flat_ranges(numel: int, world: int, row_len: int | None):
+    """Per-rank flat element intervals: FSDP2 Shard(0)-like (row-aligned) when ``row_len`` is
+    given, otherwise an even split of the flat elements (not row-aligned)."""
+    if row_len:
+        rows = numel // row_len
+        per = (rows + world - 1) // world
+        return [(min(r * per, rows) * row_len, min((r + 1) * per, rows) * row_len) for r in range(world)]
+    per = (numel + world - 1) // world
+    return [(min(r * per, numel), min((r + 1) * per, numel)) for r in range(world)]
+
+
+def _check_box(shape, box, world, row_aligned):
+    full = torch.arange(int(torch.tensor(shape).prod()), dtype=I32).view(shape)
+    e = ParamEntry("w", tuple(shape), I32, "w", 0)
+    expected = full[tuple(slice(s, s + n) for s, n in box)].contiguous() if box is not None else full
+    exp_bytes = expected.reshape(-1).numpy().tobytes()
+    got = bytearray(len(exp_bytes))
+    hit = bytearray(len(exp_bytes))
+    row_len = shape[-1] if (row_aligned and len(shape) == 2) else None
+    flat_u8 = full.reshape(-1).numpy().tobytes()
+    for f0, f1 in _flat_ranges(full.numel(), world, row_len):
+        if f0 >= f1:
+            continue
+        run = plan_box_writes(e, box, (f0 * 4, (f1 - f0) * 4))
+        # brute force: which box elements (box order) come from [f0, f1)
+        want = [i for i, v in enumerate(expected.reshape(-1).tolist()) if f0 <= v < f1]
+        if not want:
+            assert run is None
+            continue
+        assert run is not None
+        assert len(run.segments) <= 3, run.segments
+        assert want == list(range(want[0], want[-1] + 1)), "box ∩ interval must be contiguous in box order"
+        assert (run.dst_offset, run.length) == (want[0] * 4, len(want) * 4)
+        data = _gather(flat_u8[f0 * 4 : f1 * 4], run.segments)
+        assert len(data) == run.length
+        got[run.dst_offset : run.dst_offset + run.length] = data
+        assert not any(hit[run.dst_offset : run.dst_offset + run.length]), "overlapping runs"
+        hit[run.dst_offset : run.dst_offset + run.length] = b"\x01" * run.length
+    assert all(hit), "box not fully covered"
+    assert bytes(got) == exp_bytes
+

+def _tp_slices(shapes: dict, tp: int, rank: int, num_kv_heads: int, head_dim: int) -> dict:
+    """Tiny Qwen-like TP rules: q/gate/embed dim 0, o/down dim 1, k/v replicated per kv head
+    when tp > num_kv_heads, norms absent (full)."""
+    out = {}
+    for name, shape in shapes.items():
+        if name.endswith(("k_proj.weight", "v_proj.weight")):
+            if tp >= num_kv_heads:
+                blk = rank // (tp // num_kv_heads)
+                box = [[blk * head_dim, head_dim], [0, shape[1]]]
+            else:
+                n = shape[0] // tp
+                box = [[rank * n, n], [0, shape[1]]]
+        elif name.endswith(("q_proj.weight", "gate_proj.weight", "embed_tokens.weight")):
+            n = shape[0] // tp
+            box = [[rank * n, n], [0, shape[1]]]
+        elif name.endswith(("o_proj.weight", "down_proj.weight")):
+            n = shape[1] // tp
+            box = [[0, shape[0]], [rank * n, n]]
+        else:
+            continue
+        out[name] = {"full_shape": list(shape), "box": box}
+    return out
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("trainers", [1, 2, 3])

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("row_aligned", [True, False])
+def test_rank_local_end_to_end(trainers, tp, row_aligned):
+    """Full rank-local pipeline on fake buckets: rank-local layout from local shapes (one tensor
+    larger than a bucket), per-generator plans for a TP=tp replica plus a second (DP) replica,
+    dedupe across generators (merge_box_plans), pack each distinct piece once per trainer, write
+    every generator's table entries from the packed pieces, reassemble -> each generator holds
+    exactly ``full[box]`` of every tensor. Also checks the dedupe: k/v pieces are shared by
+    the TP ranks with identical boxes (num_kv_heads=2 < tp=4) and by the DP replica."""
+    torch.manual_seed(3)
+    nkv, hd, H = 2, 4, 8
+    shapes = {
+        "model.embed_tokens.weight": (16, H),
+        "model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight": (4 * hd, H),
+        "model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.weight": (nkv * hd, H),
+        "model.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj.weight": (nkv * hd, H),
+        "model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.weight": (H, 4 * hd),
+        "model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight": (96, H),  # local 48 x 8 x 4B > 1 KiB bucket at tp=2
+        "model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight": (H, 96),
+        "model.layers.0.input_layernorm.weight": (H,),
+    }
+    full = {n: torch.randn(s).to(torch.float32) for n, s in shapes.items()}
+    entries_by_src = {n: [ParamEntry(n, tuple(s), torch.float32, n, 0)] for n, s in shapes.items()}
+    bucket = 1024
+    gens = [_tp_slices(shapes, tp, r, nkv, hd) for r in range(tp)] * 2  # two TP replicas (DP=2)
+    assert len({local_shapes_key(s) for s in gens}) == 1
+    assert len({slices_digest(s) for s in gens}) == tp
+    boxes0 = normalize_slices(gens[0])
+    builder = LayoutBuilder(bucket, 256)
+    for n, (e,) in entries_by_src.items():
+        builder.add(local_entry(e, boxes0[n][1] if n in boxes0 else None))
+    layout = builder.build()
+    assert any(len(v) > 1 for v in layout.slots_by_name.values()) or tp == 4
+
+    recv = [[bytearray(bucket) for _ in range(layout.num_buckets)] for _ in gens]
+    hit = [[bytearray(bucket) for _ in range(layout.num_buckets)] for _ in gens]
+    for t in range(trainers):
+        ranges, local_u8 = {}, {}
+        for n, x in full.items():
+            row_len = x.shape[-1] if (row_aligned and x.dim() == 2) else None
+            f0, f1 = _flat_ranges(x.numel(), trainers, row_len)[t]
+            ranges[n] = (f0 * 4, (f1 - f0) * 4) if f1 > f0 else None
+            local_u8[n] = x.reshape(-1)[f0:f1].numpy().tobytes()
+        plans = [plan_rank_local_writes(entries_by_src, ranges, layout, normalize_slices(s)) for s in gens]
+        merged = merge_box_plans(plans)
+        # dedupe: no two merged pieces share a key; never more pieces than the per-gen sum
+        keys = [w.key for ws in merged.values() for w in ws]
+        assert len(keys) == len(set(keys))
+        assert len(keys) <= sum(len(ws) for p in plans for ws in p.values())
+        packed = {}
+        for src, ws in merged.items():
+            for w in ws:
+                packed[w.key] = _gather(local_u8[src], w.segments)
+                assert len(packed[w.key]) == w.length
+        for g, plan in enumerate(plans):
+            for ws in plan.values():
+                for w in ws:
+                    data = packed[w.key]  # every table entry is served from the shared pieces
+                    b = recv[g][w.bucket_id]
+                    assert not any(hit[g][w.bucket_id][w.dst_offset : w.dst_offset + w.length]), "overlap"

+async def _run(
+    backend_kwargs: dict,
+    num_trainer: int,
+    num_rollout: int,
+    bucket_size_mb: int = 128,
+    rollout_layouts=None,
+    expect_error: type | None = None,
+    num_syncs: int = 3,
+    rollout_backend_kwargs: dict | None = None,
+    rollout_tp: int = 1,
+    rank_local: bool = False,
+    model_path: str | None = None,
+    trainer_kwargs: dict | None = None,
+    retry: bool = False,
+):
+    """Run ``num_syncs`` weight syncs, checking the received weights after each one, and return
+    the per-sync metrics. With ``expect_error`` the first sync must raise it instead; with ``retry``
+    generation must then stay blocked, and the syncs run afterwards, starting at the failed step."""
+    model_path = os.path.expanduser(model_path or _model)
+    ray.init(runtime_env={"env_vars": _UCX_ENV}, ignore_reinit_error=True)
+    try:
+        ce_config = CheckpointEngineConfig(
+            backend="sharded_nixl",
+            update_weights_bucket_megabytes=bucket_size_mb,
+            engine_kwargs={"sharded_nixl": dict(backend_kwargs)},
+        )
+        rollout_ce_config = CheckpointEngineConfig(
+            backend="sharded_nixl",
+            update_weights_bucket_megabytes=bucket_size_mb,
+            engine_kwargs={"sharded_nixl": dict(rollout_backend_kwargs or backend_kwargs)},
+        )
+        model_config = HFModelConfig(path=model_path, use_remove_padding=True)
+        # RolloutConfig defaults to TP=2; each mock worker here is one TP=rollout_tp rank
+        rollout_config = RolloutConfig(
+            name="vllm", tensor_model_parallel_size=rollout_tp, checkpoint_engine=rollout_ce_config
+        )
+
+        total = num_trainer + num_rollout
+        gpus_per_node = (total + _num_nodes - 1) // _num_nodes
+        resource_pool = RayResourcePool(process_on_nodes=[gpus_per_node] * _num_nodes, max_colocate_count=3)
+        # every node gets the same bundle count; the remainder is left as an unused split
+        spare = gpus_per_node * _num_nodes - total
+        sizes = [num_trainer, num_rollout] + ([spare] if spare else [])
+        trainer_pool, rollout_pool = split_resource_pool(resource_pool, sizes)[:2]
+        actor_wg = create_trainer_worker_group(trainer_pool, model_config, ce_config, **(trainer_kwargs or {}))
+        actor_wg.reset()
+        rollout, replicas = await create_rollout_worker_group(
+            rollout_pool,
+            model_config,
+            rollout_config,
+            check_allclose=True,
+            bit_exact=True,
+            rollout_layouts=rollout_layouts,
+            rank_local=rank_local,
+        )
+        manager = CheckpointEngineManager(config=ce_config, actor_wg=actor_wg, replicas=replicas)
+        if expect_error is not None:
+            with pytest.raises(Exception) as ei:
+                await manager.update_weights(global_steps=1)
+            assert expect_error.__name__ in repr(ei.value) or isinstance(ei.value, expect_error), repr(ei.value)
+            if not retry:
+                return None
+            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="failed weight sync"):
+                await manager.resume_generation_replicas()
+        all_metrics = []
+        for step in range(num_syncs):
+            metrics = await manager.update_weights(global_steps=step + 1)
+            rollout.check_weights()
+            all_metrics.append(metrics)
+            print(f"[sharded_nixl] sync {step + 1}: {metrics}")
+        return all_metrics
+    finally:
+        ray.shutdown()

+def qwen3_tp_slices(hf_config, tp_size: int, tp_rank: int) -> dict[str, dict]:
+    """vLLM's TP slicing of dense Qwen3 (and Qwen2) as a ``RolloutLayout.slices`` table, written
+    independently of the engine's planning code.
+
+    Column-parallel (q/k/v and their Qwen2 biases, gate/up, vocab rows) splits dim 0, row-parallel
+    (o_proj, down_proj) dim 1; when tp >= num_kv_heads, ``tp // num_kv_heads`` ranks share one kv
+    head. Norms stay full.
+    """
+    cfg = hf_config
+    t, r = int(tp_size), int(tp_rank)
+    H, nh, nkv = cfg.hidden_size, cfg.num_attention_heads, cfg.num_key_value_heads
+    hd = getattr(cfg, "head_dim", None) or H // nh
+    inter, V, L = cfg.intermediate_size, cfg.vocab_size, cfg.num_hidden_layers
+    # Qwen2 configs have no attention_bias: their q/k/v always carry a bias
+    qkv_bias = getattr(cfg, "attention_bias", True)
+    assert nh % t == 0 and inter % t == 0, (nh, inter, t)
+
+    def rows(shape, n):  # dim-0 block r of size n
+        return {"full_shape": list(shape), "box": [[r * n, n], [0, shape[1]]]}
+
+    def cols(shape, n):  # dim-1 block r of size n
+        return {"full_shape": list(shape), "box": [[0, shape[0]], [r * n, n]]}
+
+    q, kv = nh * hd, nkv * hd
+    if t >= nkv:
+        assert t % nkv == 0, (t, nkv)
+        blk = r // (t // nkv)
+        kv_box = {"full_shape": [kv, H], "box": [[blk * hd, hd], [0, H]]}
+    else:
+        assert nkv % t == 0, (t, nkv)
+        kv_box = rows((kv, H), kv // t)
+    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
+    if V % t == 0:
+        for name in ("model.embed_tokens.weight", "lm_head.weight"):
+            out[name] = rows((V, H), V // t)
+    for i in range(L):
+        p = f"model.layers.{i}."
+        out[p + "self_attn.q_proj.weight"] = rows((q, H), q // t)
+        out[p + "self_attn.k_proj.weight"] = kv_box
+        out[p + "self_attn.v_proj.weight"] = kv_box
+        if qkv_bias:
+            out[p + "self_attn.q_proj.bias"] = {"full_shape": [q], "box": [[r * (q // t), q // t]]}
+            out[p + "self_attn.k_proj.bias"] = {"full_shape": [kv], "box": kv_box["box"][:1]}
+            out[p + "self_attn.v_proj.bias"] = out[p + "self_attn.k_proj.bias"]
+        out[p + "self_attn.o_proj.weight"] = cols((H, q), q // t)
+        out[p + "mlp.gate_proj.weight"] = rows((inter, H), inter // t)
+        out[p + "mlp.up_proj.weight"] = rows((inter, H), inter // t)
+        out[p + "mlp.down_proj.weight"] = cols((H, inter), inter // t)

+"""``sharded_nixl``: ownership-aware trainer -> rollout weight sync over NIXL WRITE.
+
+Every trainer rank exports only the shards it holds (``engine.get_per_tensor_param_shard`` or,
+for Megatron, ``get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard``) and WRITEs them into each generator's
+registered bucket buffers; there is no trainer-side all-gather. Each generator reports its
+``RolloutLayout`` and receives only the parameters it loads. The bucket layout follows from the
+rank-identical export order, so it is built once and cached on the generators by digest.
+Planning lives in ``sharded_nixl_layout``.
+
+Per-sync protocol (S = sync id, NB staging buffers per worker)::
+
+    generator g -> every trainer:   hello{S, rollout layout, cached layout/plan digests}   (ZMQ)
+    trainer 0   -> every generator: sync{S, layout digest, num_buckets [, full layout]}     (ZMQ)
+    trainer r   -> generator g:     plan{S, plan key, tables[k] = [(dst, len)...]}  if g lacks it (ZMQ)
+    for bucket k:
+        trainer r: wait ACK(S, k-NB) from every g; pack own slices into send_buf[k % NB];
+                   NIXL WRITE slices -> g.recv_buf[k % NB] with notif SNX{S,k,r,hashes}
+        generator: wait SNX from all trainers; verify hashes; yield tensors of bucket k;
+                   send_notif ACK{S,k} to every trainer
+
+When every generator advertises ``rank_local_named_tensors`` with slice tables of the same local
+shapes, the sync uses a second layout built from those local (box) shapes and each generator
+receives only its TP slice of each tensor.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import hashlib
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import struct
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, AsyncGenerator, Optional
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+import zmq
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.base import CheckpointEngine, CheckpointEngineRegistry, TensorMeta, merge_weight_chunks
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.nixl_checkpoint_engine import NixlAgent, NixlAgentMetadata
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.sharded_nixl_layout import (
+    DEFAULT_ALIGN,
+    BoxWriteSlice,
+    BucketLayout,
+    LayoutBuilder,
+    ParamEntry,
+    WriteSlice,
+    align_up,
+    contribution_range,
+    expand_fused_moe_entry,
+    index_runs,
+    local_entry,
+    local_shapes_key,
+    merge_box_plans,
+    normalize_slices,
+    owned_name_filter,
+    plan_indexed_writes,
+    plan_rank_local_indexed_writes,
+    plan_rank_local_writes,
+    plan_writes,
+    slices_digest,
+)
+from verl.workers.rollout.base import RolloutLayout
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))
+
+_SNX_HDR = struct.Struct("<QIII")  # sync, bucket, trainer rank, n_hashes_inline (0xFFFFFFFF: sent over ZMQ)
+_ACK_HDR = struct.Struct("<QI")  # sync, bucket
+_HASH = struct.Struct("<Q")
+
+NAMED = "named_tensors"
+RANK_LOCAL = "rank_local_named_tensors"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ShardedNixlWorkerMeta:
+    """What a worker advertises to its peers from ``prepare``."""
+
+    agent: NixlAgentMetadata
+    buffers: list[tuple[int, int, int]]  # (addr, nbytes, device id) per staging buffer
+    mem_type: str  # "VRAM" | "DRAM"
+    bucket_size: int
+    num_buffers: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _Peer:
+    """Per-peer state kept across syncs: a trainer's view of a generator, or a generator's view
+    of a trainer."""
+
+    meta: ShardedNixlWorkerMeta
+    name: str
+    rank: int
+    layout: Optional[RolloutLayout] = None
+    owns: Any = None
+    plan_key: str = ""
+    # bucket -> [(dst, len)] (named_tensors) or [(dst, len, box_key)] (rank_local_named_tensors:
+    # TP ranks share (dst, len) in the common rank-local layout but get different bytes)
+    tables: dict[int, list[tuple]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    tables_key: str = ""
+    known_digests: set = field(default_factory=set)
+    known_plan_keys: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

+
+def _hash_u8_many(t: torch.Tensor, ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
+    """One hash per ``(offset, length)`` byte range of ``t``: the XOR of the range's little-endian
+    8-byte words, the tail zero-padded, whatever the range's alignment in ``t``.
+
+    ``hash_tensor`` XORs elements, so over bytes it is only 8 bits wide; each byte lane of the
+    words is reduced separately instead.
+    """
+    word_rows, owners = [], []
+    zero_word = t.new_zeros(8)
+    for i, (offset, length) in enumerate(ranges):
+        body = length - length % 8
+        pieces = [t[offset : offset + body]] if body else []
+        if body < length:
+            pieces.append(torch.cat([t[offset + body : offset + length], zero_word[: 8 - (length - body)]]))
+        for piece in pieces:
+            word_rows.append(torch.hash_tensor(piece.view(-1, 8), dim=0))
+            owners.append(i)
+    hashes = [0] * len(ranges)
+    if word_rows:
+        for i, lanes in zip(owners, torch.stack(word_rows).tolist(), strict=True):
+            hashes[i] ^= sum(int(lane) << (8 * j) for j, lane in enumerate(lanes))
+    return hashes
+

+class ShardedNixlCheckpointEngine(CheckpointEngine):
+    """See module docstring.

+        bucket_size: staging bucket size in bytes.
+        is_master: rank 0 of the trainer group.
+        device: ``"cuda"`` (GPU staging, GPUDirect RDMA) or ``"cpu"`` (pinned host staging).
+        rollout_dtype: wire dtype for floating point tensors.
+        num_buffers: staging ring depth; must match on both sides.
+        align: byte alignment of tensors inside a bucket.
+        ownership: ``"adapter"`` (filter by the rollout worker's ``get_weight_ownership``) or
+            ``"all"`` (send every parameter to every generator).
+        notif_max_bytes: inline the per-slice hash table in the NIXL notification up to this

+    wire_format = "named_tensors"
+    send_weights_takes_engine = True

+    def __init__(

+        bucket_size: int,
+        is_master: bool = False,
+        device: str = "cuda",
+        rollout_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
+        num_buffers: int = 2,

+        ownership: str = "adapter",
+        notif_max_bytes: int = 32 << 10,
+        ack_timeout_s: float = 600.0,
+        notif_timeout_s: float = 600.0,
+        _debug_corrupt_slice: bool = False,
+        _debug_sync_offset: int = 0,
+    ) -> None:
+        assert num_buffers >= 2, "sharded_nixl needs at least 2 staging buffers"
+        assert ownership in {"all", "adapter"}, ownership
+        self.bucket_size = int(bucket_size)
+        self.is_master = is_master
+        self.device = device
+        self.mem_type = "VRAM" if device == "cuda" else "DRAM"
+        # engine_kwargs from yaml carry dtypes as strings
+        self.rollout_dtype = (
+            getattr(torch, rollout_dtype.removeprefix("torch.")) if isinstance(rollout_dtype, str) else rollout_dtype
+        )
+        self.num_buffers = int(num_buffers)
+        self.align = int(align)
+        self.ownership = ownership
+        self.notif_max_bytes = int(notif_max_bytes)
+        self.ack_timeout_s = float(ack_timeout_s)
+        self.notif_timeout_s = float(notif_timeout_s)
+        self._debug_corrupt_slice = bool(_debug_corrupt_slice)  # test hook: flips one byte after hashing, once
+        self._debug_sync_offset = int(_debug_sync_offset)  # test hook: sync-id mismatch between peers
+        self.needs_rollout_layout = ownership == "adapter"
+
+        # kept across syncs
+        self.agent: Optional[NixlAgent] = None
+        self.bufs: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+        self._buf_keepalive: list[Any] = []  # cupy arrays behind self.bufs
+        self.reg_descs: list[Any] = []
+        self.buf_descs: list[tuple[int, int, int]] = []
+        self.peers: dict[str, _Peer] = {}
+        self.peer_order: list[str] = []
+        self.role: Optional[str] = None
+        self.rank: Optional[int] = None
+        self.world_size: Optional[int] = None
+        self.num_trainers: Optional[int] = None
+        self._layout: Optional[BucketLayout] = None
+        self._plan_cache: dict[str, tuple[Optional[tuple[int, int]], list[WriteSlice]]] = {}  # src -> (range, writes)
+        self._entries_by_src: dict[str, list[ParamEntry]] = {}
+        self._uses_hf_shard_export = False
+        self._hf_runs: dict[str, list[list[tuple[int, int, int]]]] = {}  # src_name -> index_runs per entry
+        self._sync_counter = 0
+        self._rollout_layout: Optional[RolloutLayout] = None
+        self._gen_plans: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[int, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = {}  # (trainer, plan_key) -> tables
+        # rank_local_named_tensors, trainer side: local-shapes key -> layout; plan_key -> this rank's
+        # {src_name: [BoxWriteSlice]}; the deduped union for the current generator set
+        self._rl_layouts: dict[str, BucketLayout] = {}
+        self._rl_plans: dict[str, dict[str, list[BoxWriteSlice]]] = {}
+        self._rl_merged: Optional[tuple[tuple, dict[str, list[BoxWriteSlice]], int]] = None
+        self.active_wire_format = NAMED

+        self._sync_task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None  # the running send_weights / receive
+        self._inflight: dict[int, list[Any]] = {}  # bucket -> NIXL transfer handles
+        self._notifs: dict[tuple, bytes] = {}  # (peer, kind, sync, bucket) -> parked notification
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ lifecycle
+    def prepare(self) -> ShardedNixlWorkerMeta:
+        """Creates the agent and registers the staging buffers on the first call only."""
+        if self.agent is None:
+            self.agent = NixlAgent()
+        else:
+            self._drop_stale_traffic()
+        if not self.bufs:
+            self._alloc_buffers(self.bucket_size)
+        return ShardedNixlWorkerMeta(
+            agent=self.agent.get_agent_metadata(),
+            buffers=list(self.buf_descs),
+            mem_type=self.mem_type,
+            bucket_size=self.bucket_size,
+            num_buffers=self.num_buffers,
+        )
+
+    def _drop_stale_traffic(self):
+        """Drop what a failed sync left behind: its send/receive if still running, transfer handles,
+        ZMQ messages, NIXL notifications.
+
+        The manager returns as soon as one side fails, so the other side may still be waiting; left
+        running, it would race the retry for its notifications. Otherwise the next sync reads the old
+        messages first, and a retry of the same sync id can match an old ACK and overwrite a slot the
+        generator still reads. The manager runs every worker's ``prepare`` before any sync traffic,
+        so nothing current is dropped.
+        """
+        # prepare runs on the actor's event loop, so the old task cannot poll again before it unwinds
+        if self._sync_task is not None and not self._sync_task.done():
+            self._sync_task.cancel()
+        self.finalize()
+        sock = zmq.Socket.shadow(self.agent.socket.underlying)
+        while True:
+            try:
+                sock.recv(zmq.NOBLOCK)
+            except zmq.Again:
+                break
+        self.agent.messages.clear()
+        self.agent.get_new_notifs()
+
+    def _alloc_buffers(self, nbytes: int):
+        for _ in range(self.num_buffers):
+            if self.device == "cuda":
+                with patch("importlib.metadata.distributions", return_value=[]):
+                    import cupy as cp
+                # cupy allocation sidesteps the registration error torch's
+                # expandable_segments allocator causes (same trick as the nixl engine).
+                cp_buf = cp.zeros(nbytes, dtype=cp.uint8)
+                buf = torch.as_tensor(cp_buf, dtype=torch.uint8)
+                self._buf_keepalive.append(cp_buf)
+            else:
+                buf = torch.zeros(nbytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
+            self.bufs.append(buf)
+            self.reg_descs.append(self.agent.register_memory(buf))
+            dev = buf.get_device() if buf.is_cuda else 0
+            self.buf_descs.append((buf.data_ptr(), nbytes, dev))
+
+    def _free_buffers(self):
+        if self.agent is not None:
+            for rd in self.reg_descs:
+                try:
+                    self.agent.deregister_memory(rd)
+                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+                    pass
+        self.reg_descs, self.bufs, self.buf_descs, self._buf_keepalive = [], [], [], []
+
+    def _ensure_send_capacity(self, nbytes: int):
+        """Trainer only: grow the staging buffers to ``nbytes``.
+
+        In rank-local mode a trainer packs one copy per distinct box, so with T trainers and a
+        TP=t replica a bucket needs up to ~ceil(t / T) x bucket_size of staging. Generators never
+        address trainer buffers, so the advertised ``bucket_size`` is unchanged.
+        """
+        if self.bufs and self.bufs[0].numel() >= nbytes:
+            return
+        assert not self._inflight, "sharded_nixl: cannot resize staging buffers with transfers in flight"
+        new = align_up(nbytes, 1 << 20)
+        old = self.bufs[0].numel() if self.bufs else 0
+        logger.warning(f"sharded_nixl: growing trainer staging buffers {old} -> {new} bytes (rank-local)")
+        self._free_buffers()
+        self._alloc_buffers(new)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def build_topology(cls, actor_wg_world_size: int, rollout_world_size: int, metadata: list[ShardedNixlWorkerMeta]):
+        """Full bipartite topology: every trainer gets every generator's metadata and vice versa."""
+        T, G = actor_wg_world_size, rollout_world_size
+        trainer_meta, rollout_meta = list(metadata[:T]), list(metadata[T : T + G])
+        actor_wg_kwargs = {
+            "role": ["trainer"] * T,
+            "rank": list(range(T)),
+            "world_size": [T] * T,
+            "peers": [rollout_meta] * T,
+            "num_trainers": [T] * T,
+        }
+        rollout_kwargs = {
+            "role": ["rollout"] * G,
+            "rank": list(range(G)),
+            "world_size": [G] * G,
+            "peers": [trainer_meta] * G,
+            "num_trainers": [T] * G,
+        }
+        return actor_wg_kwargs, rollout_kwargs
+
+    def init_process_group(
+        self, role: str, rank: int, world_size: int, peers: list[ShardedNixlWorkerMeta], num_trainers: int
+    ):
+        """Adds new peers and drops vanished ones; existing connections are kept."""
+        self.role, self.rank, self.world_size, self.num_trainers = role, rank, world_size, num_trainers
+        new_order = []
+        seen = set()
+        for i, meta in enumerate(peers):
+            name = meta.agent.agent_name
+            seen.add(name)
+            new_order.append(name)
+            if name in self.peers:
+                self.peers[name].meta = meta
+                self.peers[name].rank = i
+            else:
+                self.agent.add_remote_agent(meta.agent)
+                self.peers[name] = _Peer(meta=meta, name=name, rank=i)
+            if meta.num_buffers != self.num_buffers or meta.bucket_size != self.bucket_size:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"sharded_nixl: peer {name} has num_buffers={meta.num_buffers}, bucket_size={meta.bucket_size}; "
+                    f"expected {self.num_buffers}/{self.bucket_size} (engine_kwargs must match on both sides)"
+                )
+        for name in list(self.peers):
+            if name not in seen:
+                self.agent.remove_remote_agent(name)
+                del self.peers[name]
+        self.peer_order = new_order
+        logger.info(f"sharded_nixl init_process_group role={role} rank={rank}/{world_size} peers={len(self.peers)}")
+
+    def finalize(self):
+        for hs in self._inflight.values():
+            for h in hs:
+                try:
+                    self.agent.release_xfer_handle(h)
+                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+                    pass
+        self._inflight = {}
+        self._notifs = {}
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ ownership
+    def set_rollout_layout(self, layout) -> None:
+        if isinstance(layout, dict):
+            layout = RolloutLayout.from_dict(layout)
+        self._rollout_layout = layout
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _plan_key(layout_digest: str, rl: Optional[RolloutLayout], wire_format: str = NAMED) -> str:
+        """Cache key of one generator's write plan: the layout plus that generator's ownership."""
+        h = hashlib.sha256(layout_digest.encode())
+        h.update(wire_format.encode())
+        if rl is not None:
+            d = rl.to_dict()
+            slices = d.pop("slices", None)
+            d["slice_digest"] = rl.slice_digest or slices_digest(slices)
+            h.update(json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True, default=list).encode())
+        return h.hexdigest()
+
+    def _choose_wire_format(self, gens: list[_Peer]) -> tuple[str, Optional[str]]:
+        """``(RANK_LOCAL, local-shapes key)`` iff every generator advertises it with the same local
+        shapes, else ``(NAMED, None)``. Deterministic in the hellos, so all trainers agree."""
+        if not gens:
+            return NAMED, None
+        keys = set()
+        for g in gens:
+            rl = g.layout
+            if rl is None or RANK_LOCAL not in (rl.wire_formats or []):
+                return NAMED, None
+            keys.add(local_shapes_key(rl.slices))
+        if len(keys) != 1:
+            logger.warning("sharded_nixl: generators disagree on rank-local shapes; falling back to named_tensors")
+            return NAMED, None
+        return RANK_LOCAL, keys.pop()
+
+    def _rank_local_layout(self, key: str, rl: RolloutLayout) -> BucketLayout:
+        """The layout of local (box) shapes, in export order; shared by generators with ``key``."""
+        lay = self._rl_layouts.get(key)
+        if lay is None:
+            boxes = normalize_slices(rl.slices)
+            builder = LayoutBuilder(self.bucket_size, self.align)
+            for entries in self._entries_by_src.values():  # insertion order == export order
+                for e in entries:
+                    spec = boxes.get(e.name)
+                    if spec is not None and tuple(spec[0]) != tuple(e.shape):
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            f"sharded_nixl: slice {e.name!r} full_shape {spec[0]} != trainer shape {e.shape}"
+                        )
+                    builder.add(local_entry(e, spec[1] if spec is not None else None))
+            lay = self._rl_layouts[key] = builder.build()
+        return lay
+
+    def _rank_local_plan(self, layout: BucketLayout, g: _Peer) -> dict[str, list[BoxWriteSlice]]:
+        plan = self._rl_plans.get(g.plan_key)
+        if plan is None:
+            boxes = normalize_slices(g.layout.slices)
+            if self._uses_hf_shard_export:
+                plan = plan_rank_local_indexed_writes(self._entries_by_src, self._hf_runs, layout, boxes, g.owns)
+            else:
+                ranges = {src: rng for src, (rng, _w) in self._plan_cache.items()}
+                plan = plan_rank_local_writes(self._entries_by_src, ranges, layout, boxes, g.owns)
+            self._rl_plans[g.plan_key] = plan
+        return plan
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _box_tables(layout: BucketLayout, plan: dict[str, list[BoxWriteSlice]]) -> dict[int, list[tuple]]:
+        tables: dict[int, list[tuple]] = {k: [] for k in range(layout.num_buckets)}
+        for ws in plan.values():
+            for w in ws:
+                tables[w.bucket_id].append((w.dst_offset, w.length, w.box_key))
+        for k in tables:
+            tables[k].sort(key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))
+        return tables
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ side channel helpers
+    async def _read(self, peer: str, typ: str, timeout: float) -> dict:
+        """The next ZMQ message from ``peer``, which must be of type ``typ`` (messages per peer are
+        FIFO, so anything else is a protocol error)."""
+        try:
+            msg = await asyncio.wait_for(self.agent.read_message(peer), timeout=timeout)
+        except asyncio.TimeoutError as e:
+            raise TimeoutError(f"sharded_nixl: timed out waiting for {typ!r} from {peer}") from e
+        if msg.get("type") != typ:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"sharded_nixl: expected {typ!r} from {peer}, got {msg.get('type')!r}")
+        return msg
+
+    async def _wait_notif(self, peer: str, kind: bytes, sync: int, k: int, timeout: float) -> bytes:
+        """Poll NIXL notifications until ``(peer, kind, sync, k)`` arrives, parking the others."""
+        key = (peer, kind, sync, k)
+        t0 = time.time()
+        while key not in self._notifs:
+            for remote, msgs in self.agent.get_new_notifs().items():
+                for m in msgs:
+                    if m[:3] == b"SNX":
+                        sync_k = _SNX_HDR.unpack_from(m, 3)[:2]
+                    elif m[:3] == b"ACK":
+                        sync_k = _ACK_HDR.unpack_from(m, 3)
+                    else:
+                        logger.warning(f"sharded_nixl: ignoring unknown notification {m[:16]!r} from {remote}")
+                        continue
+                    self._notifs[(remote, m[:3], *sync_k)] = m
+            if key in self._notifs:
+                break
+            if time.time() - t0 > timeout:
+                raise TimeoutError(f"sharded_nixl: timed out waiting for {kind!r} sync={sync} bucket={k} from {peer}")
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        return self._notifs.pop(key)
+
+    async def _wait_xfers_done(self, handles: list[Any], timeout: float):
+        t0 = time.time()
+        pending = list(handles)
+        while pending:
+            still = []
+            for h in pending:
+                st = self.agent.check_xfer_state(h)
+                if st == "ERR":
+                    raise RuntimeError("sharded_nixl: NIXL transfer failed (state ERR)")
+                if st != "DONE":
+                    still.append(h)
+            pending = still
+            if pending:
+                if time.time() - t0 > timeout:
+                    raise TimeoutError("sharded_nixl: timed out waiting for NIXL WRITE completion")
+                await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        for h in handles:
+            self.agent.release_xfer_handle(h)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ trainer side
+    def _iter_export(self, engine):
+        gen, _ = engine.get_per_tensor_param_shard()
+        return gen
+
+    def _iter_hf_export(self, engine, with_indices: bool = True):
+        gen, _ = engine.get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard(with_indices=with_indices)
+        return gen
+
+    def _model_type(self, engine) -> Optional[str]:
+        try:
+            return engine.model_config.hf_config.model_type
+        except AttributeError:
+            return None
+
+    def _wire_dtype(self, t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.dtype:
+        return self.rollout_dtype if t.is_floating_point() else t.dtype
+
+    def _hf_entries(self, src_name: str, slots, dtype_name: str) -> list[ParamEntry]:
+        """The entries of one HF-coordinate shard, in the wire dtype (the send loop casts to it)."""
+        dtype = getattr(torch, dtype_name.replace("torch.", ""))
+        dtype = self.rollout_dtype if dtype.is_floating_point else dtype
+        return [ParamEntry(name, tuple(shape), dtype, src_name) for name, shape in slots]
+
+    def _build_layout(self, engine) -> BucketLayout:
+        """First sync: one pass over the export builds the layout and this rank's write plan."""
+        if hasattr(engine, "get_per_tensor_param_hf_shard"):
+            return self._build_hf_layout(engine)
+
+        model_type = self._model_type(engine)
+        builder = LayoutBuilder(self.bucket_size, self.align)
+        entries_by_src: dict[str, list[ParamEntry]] = {}
+        plan: dict[str, tuple[Optional[tuple[int, int]], list[WriteSlice]]] = {}
+        slots_by_name: dict[str, list] = {}
+        for src_name, local, spec in self._iter_export(engine):
+            entries = expand_fused_moe_entry(src_name, tuple(spec.full_shape), self._wire_dtype(local), model_type)
+            entries_by_src[src_name] = entries
+            for e in entries:
+                slots_by_name[e.name] = builder.add(e)
+            rng = contribution_range(spec, local.numel(), entries[0].itemsize)
+            plan[src_name] = (rng, plan_writes(slots_by_name, entries, rng) if rng is not None else [])
+            del local
+        layout = builder.build()
+        self._entries_by_src = entries_by_src
+        self._plan_cache = plan
+        return layout
+
+    def _build_hf_layout(self, engine) -> BucketLayout:
+        """Build the layout from backend-converted HF-coordinate shards."""
+        builder = LayoutBuilder(self.bucket_size, self.align)
+        entries_by_src: dict[str, list[ParamEntry]] = {}
+        for src_name, slots, dtype_name, counts, indices, values, _group in self._iter_hf_export(engine):
+            entries = self._hf_entries(src_name, slots, dtype_name)
+            entries_by_src[src_name] = entries
+            for entry in entries:
+                builder.add(entry)
+            del counts, indices, values
+        layout = builder.build()
+        self._entries_by_src = entries_by_src
+        self._plan_cache = {}
+        for src_name, slots, dtype_name, counts, indices, values, _group in self._iter_hf_export(engine):
+            runs = self._hf_runs[src_name] = index_runs(counts, indices)
+            self._plan_cache[src_name] = (None, plan_indexed_writes(layout, entries_by_src[src_name], runs))
+            del slots, dtype_name, counts, indices, values
+        self._uses_hf_shard_export = True
+        return layout
+
+    def _tables_for(self, layout: BucketLayout, owns) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, int]]]:
+        """Per-bucket sorted ``(dst, len)`` of this rank's writes to a generator with ``owns``."""
+        tables: dict[int, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {k: [] for k in range(layout.num_buckets)}
+        for _src, (_rng, slices) in self._plan_cache.items():
+            for s in slices:
+                if owns(s.name):
+                    tables[s.bucket_id].append((s.dst_offset, s.length))
+        for k in tables:
+            tables[k].sort()
+        return tables
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    async def send_weights(self, engine, global_steps: int | None = None) -> dict[str, float] | None:
+        """Send this rank's shards; metrics are returned on rank 0 only."""
+        assert self.role == "trainer", f"send_weights called on role={self.role}"
+        self._sync_task = asyncio.current_task()
+        t_start = time.time()
+        S = (global_steps if global_steps is not None else self._sync_counter) + self._debug_sync_offset
+        # counted per attempt on both sides, so a sync that fails on one side only does not split them
+        self._sync_counter += 1
+        gens = [self.peers[n] for n in self.peer_order]
+        nb = self.num_buffers
+
+        # 0. hellos: ownership + caches of every generator
+        hello_bytes = 0
+        for g in gens:
+            msg = await self._read(g.name, "hello", self.notif_timeout_s)
+            if msg["sync"] != S:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"sharded_nixl: generator {g.name} is at sync {msg['sync']}, trainer at {S}")
+            g.layout = RolloutLayout.from_dict(msg.get("layout"))
+            g.owns = owned_name_filter(g.layout)
+            g.known_digests = set(msg.get("known_digests", []))
+            g.known_plan_keys = dict(msg.get("known_plan_keys", {}))
+            hello_bytes += len(json.dumps(msg, default=str))
+
+        # 1. layout: built on the first sync, then validated against the export below
+        first_sync = self._layout is None
+        if first_sync:
+            self._layout = self._build_layout(engine)
+        full_layout = layout = self._layout
+        wire_format, rl_key = self._choose_wire_format(gens)
+        if self.is_master and wire_format != self.active_wire_format:
+            logger.info(f"sharded_nixl: wire format {self.active_wire_format} -> {wire_format}")
+        self.active_wire_format = wire_format
+        if wire_format == RANK_LOCAL:
+            layout = self._rank_local_layout(rl_key, gens[0].layout)
+
+        # 2. sync header (rank 0) and this rank's write tables, for generators that lack them
+        meta_bytes = 0
+        my_name = self.agent.agent_name
+        for g in gens:
+            g.plan_key = self._plan_key(layout.digest, g.layout, wire_format)
+            if self.rank == 0:
+                msg = {
+                    "type": "sync",
+                    "sync": S,
+                    "digest": layout.digest,
+                    "num_buckets": layout.num_buckets,
+                    "num_trainers": self.num_trainers,
+                    "wire_format": wire_format,
+                }
+                if layout.digest not in g.known_digests:
+                    msg["layout"] = layout.to_wire()
+                self.agent.send_message(g.name, msg)
+                meta_bytes += _approx_size(msg)
+
+        # 3. export pass: pack and WRITE bucket by bucket. Export order == layout order on every
+        #    rank, so a bucket can be flushed as soon as a slice of a later bucket shows up.
+        stats = {"payload": 0, "meta": 0}
+        my_dev = self.buf_descs[0][2]
+        pending: list[tuple[WriteSlice | BoxWriteSlice, torch.Tensor]] = []
+        for g in gens:
+            if g.tables_key != g.plan_key:
+                if wire_format == RANK_LOCAL:
+                    g.tables = self._box_tables(layout, self._rank_local_plan(layout, g))
+                else:
+                    g.tables = self._tables_for(layout, g.owns)
+                g.tables_key = g.plan_key
+            if g.known_plan_keys.get(my_name) != g.plan_key:
+                # the generator only needs (dst, len) per slice (its own box is implied)
+                wire_tables = {k: [(t[0], t[1]) for t in v] for k, v in g.tables.items()}
+                msg = {"type": "plan", "sync": S, "plan_key": g.plan_key, "rank": self.rank, "tables": wire_tables}
+                self.agent.send_message(g.name, msg)
+                stats["meta"] += _approx_size(msg)
+        box_plan: dict[str, list[BoxWriteSlice]] = {}
+        if wire_format == RANK_LOCAL:
+            # One packed copy per distinct (bucket, dst, len, box): DP replicas and replicated k/v
+            # heads share pieces. Size the staging buffers for the fullest bucket.
+            mkey = tuple(g.plan_key for g in gens)
+            if self._rl_merged is None or self._rl_merged[0] != mkey:
+                box_plan = merge_box_plans(self._rank_local_plan(layout, g) for g in gens)
+                per_bucket: dict[int, int] = {}
+                for ws in box_plan.values():
+                    for w in ws:
+                        # + the worst-case 8-byte padding: _flush packs in export order, not this one
+                        per_bucket[w.bucket_id] = per_bucket.get(w.bucket_id, 0) + w.length + 7
+                self._rl_merged = (mkey, box_plan, max(per_bucket.values(), default=0))
+            _mk, box_plan, need = self._rl_merged
+            self._ensure_send_capacity(need)
+
+        async def _flush(k: int, items: list[tuple[WriteSlice, torch.Tensor]]):
+            """Pack this rank's part of bucket ``k`` and WRITE it to every generator."""
+            slot = k % nb
+            if k >= nb:
+                # the slot's previous bucket must be written and ACKed by every generator

+"""Static bucket layout and write planning for the ``sharded_nixl`` checkpoint engine.
+
+Pure planning, no transfers. Every trainer rank exports its local shard of every parameter in
+the same order (``engine.get_per_tensor_param_shard()``), so every rank computes the same
+:class:`BucketLayout` from the ``(name, full_shape, dtype)`` sequence without communicating.
+A flat-contiguous shard (FSDP2 ``Shard(0)``, replicated, HSDP) is one byte interval of the
+flattened tensor, so each rank's part of a bucket is a few :class:`WriteSlice` objects and the
+generator's bucket holds the full tensors once every trainer has written.
+
+Fused MoE parameters are expanded into the per-expert HF names vLLM loads, mirroring
+``verl.workers.engine.fsdp.utils.unfuse_moe_params``; each expert is a contiguous sub-range of
+the fused tensor, so expansion only relabels byte ranges.

+class ParamEntry:
+    """One HF tensor as the generator loads it. Element ``i`` of the entry is element
+    ``src_elem_offset + i`` of the flattened exported tensor ``src_name`` (several entries share
+    one source for a fused MoE tensor)."""

+    name: str
+    shape: tuple[int, ...]
+    dtype: torch.dtype
+    src_name: str
+    src_elem_offset: int = 0

+    @property

+        n = 1
+        for d in self.shape:

+    @property
+    def itemsize(self) -> int:
+        return torch.empty(0, dtype=self.dtype).element_size()

+    @property
+    def nbytes(self) -> int:
+        return self.numel * self.itemsize
+
+    @property
+    def src_byte_offset(self) -> int:
+        return self.src_elem_offset * self.itemsize
+
+    def key(self) -> tuple:
+        return (self.name, tuple(int(d) for d in self.shape), str(self.dtype))
